provenance: Lane split authored by the Stage-2 decision-agent (read-only; returns JSON in reply) and persisted by the orchestrator as the agent's returned detect-vs-hunt partition. Detection = seed complement of the agent's hunt set; validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup, and det-count reconciled against the agent's summary. All ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset. Per-technique rationale shows the Stage-1 detection-feasibility basis.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — Exchange/ProxyShell/ProxyLogon exploitation is detectable via appliance/IIS logs, patch-level telemetry, and known exploit signatures, though n-day edge exploitation often precedes visibility
high — new .aspx files under web-root paths and w3wp.exe/IIS worker spawning child processes are strong, well-covered detection signals

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: high — new-service creation (Event ID 7045 / Services registry writes) registering an unknown driver/service such as DCUMSrv or DCDrv is highly detectable
high — scheduled-task creation (Event ID 4698) with a spoofed browser-agent name pointing at an unusual binary is a strong, anomalous signal

medium — remote PowerShell execution to push payloads to peers is detectable via script-block logging (4104), 4688/Sysmon process telemetry and remote-execution patterns, though PowerShell is heavily used by admins
medium — WMIC-based remote process creation is detectable via WMI-activity logs and wmic.exe command-line telemetry, but overlaps with legitimate administration
high — PsExec creates a named service and PSEXESVC on the target (Event ID 7045 / named-pipe activity), a well-covered remote-execution signal

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — cmd.exe spawned by an anomalous parent (a RAT masquerading as calc.exe) is detectable via parent-child process analytics
medium — the file-copy-of-genuine-calc-then-delete-of-RAT sequence is detectable via EDR file-create/delete telemetry, though self-deletion overlaps with benign cleanup
medium — admin-share writes of executables followed by remote service creation are detectable via SMB file-write and 5140/7045 correlation
medium — internal copies of a novel executable to multiple hosts over SMB are detectable via file-write telemetry, though they ride trusted admin channels
medium — regular fixed-interval HTTP beaconing to a low-reputation domain with recurring /RVP/index*.php URIs is detectable via network beacon analytics and proxy logs
medium — the RAT process fetching and writing new executable modules is detectable via process-network-then-file-write correlation
medium — a user-mode/service process obtaining raw disk access to overwrite the boot-loader/MBR is a rare, high-fidelity destructive signal detectable via raw-disk-write / driver-load EDR analytics

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — off-victim capability development is not observable in defender telemetry; value is retrospective attribution via code/PDB/DiskCryptor-fork overlap analysis of recovered samples

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — name-matching masquerade evades name-based rules; hunt candidate via original-filename (PE VERSIONINFO) vs on-disk-name mismatch and calc.exe/svchost.exe running from non-standard paths

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — an embedded encrypted payload is opaque until runtime extraction; hunt candidate via entropy/PyInstaller-artifact analysis of the sample rather than host log detection
low — use of legitimate admin credentials blends with normal activity; hunt candidate via a single account authenticating to many hosts in a short window paired with service creation
low — host-profiling API/command activity is high-volume and mostly benign; hunt candidate only in correlation with the surrounding intrusion chain
low — domain host enumeration blends with legitimate administration; hunt candidate via enumeration immediately preceding mass remote execution
low — file/directory enumeration is ubiquitous benign activity; only meaningful in RAT-behavior correlation
low — screen-capture APIs are used by many legitimate apps; not reliably detectable in isolation, hunt only via RAT-behavior clustering
low — local file reads are high-volume normal activity; hunt candidate via bulk-access-then-stage-then-exfil sequencing
low — XOR-obfuscated payloads defeat plaintext content inspection; hunt candidate via traffic-shape/beacon analytics and static key extraction from recovered samples
low — exfil to web/Telegram services blends with normal web traffic; hunt candidate via large outbound transfers to file-sharing/messaging endpoints from server hosts

low — full-volume encryption via a legitimate signed disk-crypto driver produces little conventional file-rename/entropy signal and is often unrecoverable regardless; hunt the precursors (DCUMSrv/DCDrv service creation, PsExec/WMIC spread, DiskCryptor driver load)
low — by the time destruction is observable the impact has occurred; detection value is entirely in the earlier chain (web shell, credential reuse, lateral spread, driver/service install)
low — a reboot call is trivially common and only meaningful as the terminal step of the encrypt/boot-overwrite chain; hunt via correlation with preceding raw-disk-write and service-install events
